chunks: That was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about exchanging two worn garments for one superior garment, and one camel for two camels, and one beast of burden for two beasts of burden. He said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) disliked that, so we dislike it, unless the two types differ.' He said: 'And I asked him about camels, cattle, and sheep, or one of them in this regard, and he said: "Yes, we dislike it."'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging two inferior items for one superior item of the same type in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith traces the juristic preference (*karahah*) for unequal exchange of same-category goods back to Imam Ali (AS), establishing a foundational principle in Shia commercial jurisprudence. The narration clarifies that this aversion applies strictly when the items are of the same variety (*sinf*), but allows for flexibility if the types differ, thereby distinguishing between *riba al-fadl* (excess in exchange) and simple barter. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on fairness and transparency in trade, preventing hidden disparities that could lead to dispute or exploitation.
